title: Transfer Factor for Homes Moved from Tidemark's NFIP Book to HomeFlood
content:
**Purpose.** The NFIP transfer factor of a HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies re-rated term premium, worked out when an Elevation Certificate review is completed, recognises a home moved from Tidemark's federal book. That book is the NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own).

**The NFIP record.** The customer's NFIP record for the address is the Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy this HomeFlood policy replaced — the one whose policy number is the policy's replaced NFIP policy number. A HomeFlood policy that replaced no NFIP policy has no NFIP record.

**The rule.** The run of the NFIP record is counted in whole calendar months from its original effective date to its cancellation effective date. A count of whole calendar months runs from the earlier date to the later one; the last month is not counted when the later date's day of the month falls before the earlier date's day of the month.

| The NFIP record | Run | Transfer factor |
|---|---|---|
| cancelled for the reason replaced by private flood | at least 120 whole months | 1 minus 4 percent, that is 0.96 |
| cancelled for the reason replaced by private flood | fewer than 120 whole months | 1 minus 2 percent, that is 0.98 |
| cancelled for another reason, or no NFIP record | — | 1 |

**Records read.** The factor is read from the NFIP Dwelling Form policy record: its original effective date, its cancellation reason and its cancellation effective date.

**How the factor applies.** The transfer factor multiplies the rate amount of the re-rated term premium along with its zone, elevation and deductible factors. It applies before any credit reduction and before the loss-of-use charge is added.

## Hypothetical cases

- NFIP coverage ran from 15 April of one year to 15 April ten years later, then was cancelled for replacement by private flood. The run is 120 whole months, so the factor is 0.96.
- The same record cancelled on 14 April ten years later runs 119 whole months, so the factor is 0.98.
- A HomeFlood policy issued with no replaced NFIP policy number has a factor of 1.
